docs_quotes: Add the `eleventyNavigation` object to your front matter data (or in a [data directory file](https://www.11ty.io/docs/data-template-dir/)). Assign a unique string to the `key` property inside of `eleventyNavigation`.
Any templates that do not have `parent` will be assumed to be at the top level.
To nest a template inside of the Mammals template, use `parent: Mammals`:
To ensure that Humans comes first before Bats, use the `order` property. It can have an arbitrary number. If omitted, `order: 0` is the default.
The `eleventyNavigation` filter returns a _sorted_ array of objects with `url` and `title` properties (sorted using `order`, as noted above).
If you want your key and your link text to be different, use the `title` property:
Note that you can also pass any collection into `eleventyNavigation`. It doesn’t have to be `collections.all`!

In front matter (or further upstream in the data cascade), set the `eleventyExcludeFromCollections` option to true to opt out of specific pieces of content added to all collections (including `collections.all`, collections set using tags, or collections added from the Configuration API in your config file).
This will not be available in `collections.all` or `collections.post`.
The default collection sorting algorithm sorts in ascending order using:
1. The input file’s Created Date (you can override using `date` in front matter, as shown below)
2. Files created at the exact same time are tie-broken using the input file’s full path including filename

grouping.how_sections_are_formed: Via the `parent` property: "To nest a template inside of the Mammals template, use `parent: Mammals`" — the parent value names the `key` of the section to join. "Any templates that do not have `parent` will be assumed to be at the top level."
grouping.section_order_rule: The docs state no separate ordering rule for sections/children; the Re-Ordering Items example nests with `parent` and orders the children with the same `order` property (Humans `order: 1`, Bats `order: 2`, both `parent: Mammals`), and the filter is described as "sorted using `order`".

inclusion.what_hides_it: "In front matter (or further upstream in the data cascade), set the `eleventyExcludeFromCollections` option to true to opt out of specific pieces of content added to all collections (including `collections.all`, collections set using tags, or collections added from the Configuration API in your config file)." ("This will not be available in `collections.all` or `collections.post`.") A page not present in the collection passed to the filter is not rendered, since the menu is built from the filter input: "Note that you can also pass any collection into `eleventyNavigation`. It doesn’t have to be `collections.all`!"
inclusion.what_makes_a_page_appear_in_nav: "Add the `eleventyNavigation` object to your front matter data (or in a [data directory file](https://www.11ty.io/docs/data-template-dir/)). Assign a unique string to the `key` property inside of `eleventyNavigation`." The menu is rendered from a collection passed through the filter, e.g. `collections.all | eleventyNavigation`, so the page must also be present in that collection.

ordering.primary_key: eleventyNavigation.order — "To ensure that Humans comes first before Bats, use the `order` property. It can have an arbitrary number." The filter output is "a _sorted_ array of objects with `url` and `title` properties (sorted using `order`, as noted above)."
ordering.tie_break: The docs do not say what happens when two pages share the same order value.

undocumented: Tie-break rule when two pages share the same `order` value — the docs never state it (the sort comparator is only described as "sorted using `order`").

How an omitted `order` compares against explicit positive or negative orders in practice — the docs say only "If omitted, `order: 0` is the default," without showing a mixed example or stating whether missing behaves exactly like literal 0.

Whether `key` is strictly required for an entry to appear — the docs say to "Assign a unique string to the `key` property" but never state what happens to an `eleventyNavigation` object with no `key`.
What happens with duplicate `key` values — uniqueness is instructed ("Assign a unique string") but no behavior for duplicates is documented.
What happens when `parent` names a key that does not exist (orphaned child) — not addressed.

Whether `title` falls back to `key` when omitted — the prose only says "If you want your key and your link text to be different, use the `title` property"; the fallback is demonstrated in the example JSON output ({"key": "Mammals", "title": "Mammals"} with only `key` set) but never stated in normative text.

Whether `draft: true` removes a page from the nav — neither the navigation docs nor the collections docs page mentions drafts; draft exclusion in the starter comes from the starter's own `addPreprocessor` config, not from documented nav/collection behavior.
The word "ascending" for nav order direction — direction is demonstrated by example (Humans `order: 1` before Bats `order: 2`) but never stated literally.
Any separate ordering rule for sections (children) versus top-level items — no distinct rule is documented.
The plugin's `pinned` property and its effect on sorting — not mentioned anywhere in these docs pages (present only in the plugin implementation).
The docs page itself notes it is stale: "This documentation is for `eleventy-navigation` `v0.3.x`." while the tested plugin is v1.0.5, so documented behavior may lag the implementation.
